problem: Existing VLN pre-training does not systematically exploit cross-modal semantic alignment between instructions, trajectories and observations, which limits how well the agent understands its own state during navigation.
motivation: Semantic alignment across modalities is crucial for the agent to interpret instructions and current visual observations and choose correct actions. Better-aligned representations give a consistent perception of the environment and make actions easier to explain.
key_idea: Introduce a Latent Semantic Alignment Learning framework with three pre-training tasks (Trajectory-conditioned Masked Fragment Modeling, Action Prediction of Masked Observation, Hierarchical Triple Contrastive Learning) to learn cross-modal dependencies and semantically consistent representations.
insight: From the abstract only: explicitly modeling cross-modal dependencies (the first two tasks) and enforcing consistent representations across modalities (the third task) improves over the baseline model, with gains of 1.6% SR on R2R val-unseen and 4.3% SR on R4R val-unseen. No ablation details are available.
method: Trajectory-conditioned Masked Fragment Modeling: pre-training task that masks fragments and reconstructs them conditioned on the trajectory to reason about cross-modal dependencies.
Action Prediction of Masked Observation: pre-training task that predicts the action when the observation is masked, reasoning about cross-modal dependencies.
Hierarchical Triple Contrastive Learning: contrastive pre-training across three modalities at multiple levels to learn semantically consistent representations.

setting.training_data: pre-training with three proposed tasks (details not available in abstract)

results: On R2R val-unseen the method improves SR by 1.6% over the baseline model, and on R4R val-unseen by 4.3%. Absolute numbers and comparisons to other methods are not available from the abstract.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details on experiments, baselines and limitations are unknown.
